title: Omaha to Bozeman, a family of four, the week before Christmas
covers: Long drive with one night; family with two children; thirsty car; winter pass; no nonstop (one connection); medium to small airport; parking; two checked bags; rental at the destination; crosses a time zone

fare.source: southwest.com route page (Basic fare, via Denver)

rental.source: Kayak, BZN December average (start not used: own car)

105 min for seven 15-minute stops with children, about every 2½ hours (Claude's call)
90 min for two lunch stops on the road, 45 minutes each with children (Claude's call)
Dinner on day one is in Spearfish, SD after checking in, so it adds no road time
45 min getting off the road, checking in, and loading the car in the morning (Claude's call)
20 min expected weather slowdown over Bozeman Pass in December (Claude's call)

notes: Southwest has no nonstop on this route, so DOT has no scheduled time for it; `schedule` is null and the fare carries the itinerary's length and one stop.
The 2:15 p.m. arrival time in Bozeman is on Omaha's clock, an hour ahead of Bozeman's.
Kayak, Hertz, and Cheapflights gave $135, $169, and $231 as Bozeman's December daily rental average. Kayak's is used; it's the biggest swing in this trip's cost.
The Basic fare is the lowest shown for one traveler. Four seats at that price on one flight isn't guaranteed this close to the holidays.
The route crosses US 212 through rural northeast Wyoming and southeast Montana, with long gaps between services in winter. That's for Our take to weigh, not the numbers.
The family parks at OMA for eight days, until the drive home after Christmas; only the outbound trip is compared.
